note: Six synthetic incidents, written the way a driver would say them out loud. The truth sheet beside each one is what a correct draft has to contain, decided here rather than after seeing what any model produced. Nothing in these is real: no policy, no vehicle, no person, no place beyond an invented street.

scenarios.brief: A delivery van reversed into my car while it was parked in the car park on Harbour Road. It caught the left front wing and left a dent. The car still drives, and it is still there in the Harbour Road car park.
scenarios.why_this_one: The common case, and the one the page opens on. Nothing conditional fires.

scenarios.brief: Someone backed into me at the supermarket and scraped the rear bumper. It is a scratch, nothing worse. The car is fine to drive and it is on my drive at home now.
scenarios.why_this_one: A different panel and the lightest severity, so a run cannot pass by memorising S1.

scenarios.brief: I hit a bollard head on coming out of a junction. The front is caved in and the car will not drive, it is sitting at the junction of Mill Lane and Rope Street where it stopped.
scenarios.why_this_one: The car is off the road AND the damage is structural, so Northwind raises the roadside collection, the collection address and the police report reference at once. A static form knows about none of the three.

scenarios.brief: A car came through a give way sign and hit my passenger side. The wheel is pointing the wrong way and I cannot drive it. It is outside number 40 on Cross Street.
scenarios.why_this_one: The same conditional pair as S3 from a different side of the car, so the result is not one scenario's accident.

scenarios.brief: My car was taken overnight from the street outside my house. I reported it to the police this morning and they gave me a reference, CR-4471-B. There is nothing to describe about damage because the car is gone.
scenarios.why_this_one: Theft is the case where Northwind asks for a police report reference and does not ask where the impact landed. It is also the case the original filing defect got wrong.

scenarios.brief: A lorry clipped my nearside rear as it pulled out. The panel is pushed in badly and the door frame is bent, but I drove it home and it is on my drive.
scenarios.why_this_one: Structural damage on a car that still drives. The police report requirement fires on severity alone, and the collection requirements do not, which no static form can distinguish.
